planting.note: Allow cuttings to dry and callus for 1-2 weeks before planting in extremely well-drained, sandy soil in full sun; Kimo is a Hawaiian-bred cultivar with wide, round, heavily overlapping petals in strong orange and yellow banded with moderate pink on both faces.

directions: Root cuttings in extremely well-drained, sandy soil in full sun after letting the cut end callus for one to two weeks before setting it in the ground or pot. Kimo was bred by Hawaiian plumeria hobbyist Ted Chinn and named for his father; it produces three-inch, wide-petaled flowers in strong orange and yellow with moderate pink banding on both the front and back of the petals, carried on a vigorous, medium-growing tree. The blooms are noted for long vase and lei life and a sweet, lemon-lime-tinged fragrance that carries well in the evening garden. Because it is a deciduous Plumeria rubra selection, plants drop their leaves and go fully dormant in winter; in zone 9a, lift container plants or move them to an unheated, frost-free garage before the first hard freeze and withhold water until new growth resumes in spring.
sources: Plumeria Society of America — Cultivar Registry (PSA Reg. #118)
University of Florida IFAS Extension — Plumeria Culture

common_name: Grove Farm Plumeria (Deep Pink-and-Red Fragrant Hawaiian Plumeria)

planting.note: Allow cuttings to dry and callus for 1-2 weeks before planting in extremely well-drained, sandy soil in full sun; Grove Farm, named for the historic Kauai plantation, bears large moderate-pink flowers with a bright yellow center and strong red petal bands.

directions: Root cuttings in extremely well-drained, sandy soil in full sun, letting the cut surface callus for one to two weeks before planting. Grove Farm, an old-line Hawaiian cultivar named for the Grove Farm sugar plantation on Kauai, produces large four-to-four-and-a-half-inch flowers in moderate pink with a brilliant small yellow center and bold red bands running up both the front and back of the wide, grainy-textured petals. It is an upright, structurally strong, reliable repeat bloomer prized by lei makers for the unusual rose-and-nutmeg edge to its fragrance alongside the classic plumeria sweetness. As a deciduous Plumeria rubra selection it drops its leaves and needs a completely dry winter rest; in zone 9a, move container specimens to a frost-free, unheated space and keep the soil dry until regrowth appears in spring, since cold combined with wet roots is the most common killer of overwintered plumeria.
sources: Plumeria Society of America — Cultivar Registry (PSA Reg. #128)
University of Florida IFAS Extension — Plumeria Culture

common_name: Dwarf Deciduous Plumeria (Khao Bali White Fragrant Frangipani)

planting.note: Allow cuttings to dry and callus for 1-2 weeks before planting in extremely well-drained, sandy soil in full sun; also sold as Khao Bali, this compact, well-branched selection bears large snow-white flowers with a small golden-yellow center and faint pink banding on the petal reverse.

directions: Root cuttings in extremely well-drained, sandy soil in full sun after allowing the cut end to callus for one to two weeks. Despite the name, Dwarf Deciduous (also traded as Khao Bali) is not a true miniature but a compact, densely branched grower that stays more manageable in a pot than standard tree-form plumeria, while still producing some of the largest blooms in the dwarf-type group at four to five inches across, in bright snow white with a small golden-yellow center and soft pink bands on the back of the petals. Its strong, sweet citrus fragrance is most noticeable in the evening, and the plant tends to bloom continuously through the warm season rather than in a single flush. It is more cold-tender than many standard plumeria and holds its foliage later into fall before dropping it for winter dormancy; in zone 9a, bring containers into an unheated, frost-free space well before the first freeze and keep the soil dry until new leaves emerge in spring.
sources: Plumeria Society of America — Cultivar Registry
University of Florida IFAS Extension — Plumeria Culture

common_name: Siam Rainbow Plumeria (Multi-Color White-Pink-Yellow Thai Frangipani)

planting.note: Allow cuttings to dry and callus for 1-2 weeks before planting in extremely well-drained, sandy soil in full sun; this Thai-bred compact cultivar blends white, pink, and yellow genetically within each flower rather than through grafting, and the pattern is reproduced true from cuttings.

directions: Root cuttings in extremely well-drained, sandy soil in full sun, letting the cut surface callus for one to two weeks before planting. Siam Rainbow is a compact Thai cultivar whose three-inch flowers blend white, pink, and yellow within the same bloom as a fixed genetic trait, unlike the multi-color effect created by grafting several different cultivars onto one rootstock; propagating from cuttings of the named plant reliably reproduces the same color pattern, while seedlings from its pods will not. It carries a fresh, lively citrus fragrance and blooms repeatedly through the warm season on a manageable, slower-growing plant well suited to containers. Give it the same lean, fast-draining mix and full sun that other plumeria need, and avoid soggy soil, which quickly leads to stem rot in cooler weather. In zone 9a it must be grown in a container and moved to an unheated, frost-free space for winter dormancy, since this compact selection has no more cold tolerance than other tropical Plumeria rubra cultivars.
sources: Plumeria Society of America — Cultivar Registry
